coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 101 (Bethlehem Steel HQ)
names: RH San Francisco, The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building
record.summary: The 1917 Classical Revival main office of the Union Iron Works at the corner of 20th and Illinois Streets, designed by Frederick H. Meyer, rehabilitated by Orton Development under the Port's 66-year Historic Core master lease and subleased whole to RH (Restoration Hardware) on a 41-year sublease from February 2017; RH San Francisco, with the Palm Court restaurant and a rooftop park, opened May 13, 2022.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself. The match to 'Building 101' specifically (as opposed to a neighboring structure) rests on position (33.9m from the diagram's own label, closest of any candidate) and shape correspondence, not an address or explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself, since no such attribute exists there.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4046001) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll, and the building's own press addresses do not resolve to any DataSF parcel either. The real Assessor lot groups 5 named buildings (101, 102, 104, 122, 123) into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Bethlehem Steel HQ, a 1917 neoclassical office building designed by Frederick H. Meyer, ~80,000 sf, 5 floors plus 2 lower levels and a penthouse. Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) starting after a Nov 26 2013 Historic Preservation Commission review (sfplanning.org HPC packet 2013.1168E); per that packet, the seismic upgrade uses shear walls, and the rehab preserves the historic exterior elevations while adapting the interior. Completed in stages ~2017-2020. Now houses RH San Francisco -- 'The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building' (showroom, Palm Court restaurant, rooftop bar), opened May 2022.

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
Classical Revival; three stories with basement (plus sub-basement), concrete and brick, stucco-clad, L-shaped with a beveled corner entry
140 ft 6 in by 51 ft 10 in by 72 ft high (NRHP); 140 ft by 50 ft, 72 ft in D4D Figure 6.5.4
56,268 (NRHP); 61,311 before and 60,525 after rehabilitation, plus a 9,000 sq ft new restaurant building behind it (Port 2019 Table 1); RH describes ~80,000 sq ft over five floors
RH (Restoration Hardware): RH San Francisco gallery, Palm Court restaurant, wine bars, rooftop park
James Gillam, Backen, Gillam & Kroeger (RH's design architect)
Reinforced concrete shear walls; interior partitions removed for an open floor plan (2013 HPC packet)
Union Iron Works / Bethlehem Steel main office; vacant before rehabilitation, formerly office use and one residential unit
All of Building 101 and the new restaurant north of it are listed by the Port as publicly accessible spaces under Master Lease Exhibit K

open_questions: The exact completion / certificate of occupancy date for Building 101 (the Port's 2019 memo anticipated 2020; RH opened May 2022) was not found.

Whether Buildings 122 and 123, the two outbuildings behind Building 104 that share the master lease, are on this parcel or the Building 104 parcel is not settled by any source; this repo's status.csv groups them with the north-side lot.
No 'now' photograph with a stated license was found; RH's press images are the tenant's copyright and are linked, not hosted.
The HAER survey named in the brief was not located in the Library of Congress catalog (see PR description); the NRHP nomination is used as the historic primary source.
